title: LDD Y+q misdecoded when d>=16
description: The mask `(word & 0x0200) == 0` treats the destination register's MSB as opcode, so any LDD with d>=16 is rejected even though it is a valid encoding.

title: LDD Z+q misdecoded when d>=16
description: Same incorrect `(word & 0x0200) == 0` guard rejects valid LDD Rd,Z+q when the destination register has bit 4 set.

title: BSET/BCLR shadowed by SEC/CLC etc.
description: decode_avr_fixed claims 0x9408..0x94F8 first, so the generic BSET/BCLR arms in decode_avr_alu2 are unreachable, hiding the bit-index operand form.

title: JMP/CALL absolute target multiplied by 2
description: AVR JMP/CALL encodes a word address; `target = ((k_hi<<16)|k_lo) * 2` doubles the byte address, producing wrong targets above 64 KiB.

title: Branch target parsed without bounding to program memory
description: `u64::from_str_radix` accepts any width hex and `get_branches` returns the raw value, so a wrapped negative rel_target (e.g., RJMP -1 at PC=0) yields a bogus ~2^64 branch target.

title: `bytes[..dec.size.min(bytes.len())]` masks truncation
description: If decode_avr returns a 4-byte size but the caller passed only 2 bytes (e.g., end of buffer) the size field still says 4 while raw is 2 — downstream code that trusts `instr.size` advances past EOF.

title: Backward-jump loop detector misses self-loop
description: `target < i` excludes a jump-to-self (target == i), so infinite self-loops are not flagged as loops/unbounded.

title: Bounds check casts negative base/offset to u64
description: `offset as u64` and `base as u64 + len` wrap negative i64 to enormous u64, making `check_bounds` return Safe for cases that should be Unsafe when base/offset are negative but not strictly less than each other.

title: Jump target cast from i64 to usize without negative check
description: `(pc as i64 + 1 + insn.off as i64) as usize` wraps to huge usize on negative result; subsequent `< program.len()` check still treats it as out-of-bounds error rather than ignoring, but a backward jump (off negative making target valid) is silently treated as forward visit and may not enqueue the real backward target — back-edges to PC 0 work only by coincidence.

title: Field reloc ignores access string and always uses members[0]
description: `apply` for FieldByteOffset/FieldByteSize patches the immediate with the FIRST member regardless of the parsed access indices, silently producing wrong offsets for any field other than the first.

title: Fat section data_size u24 decoded with wrong byte placement
description: Using `from_le_bytes([0, bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]])` shifts each byte up by 8 bits, producing a value 256x too large and an inflated clause count.

title: Stream header loop indexes `data[off..]` without bounds check
description: If `off` exceeds `data.len()` after a previous iteration, slicing panics instead of returning an error.

title: stream_data computes `start + size` without checked_add
description: On 32-bit or with huge attacker-controlled size, addition wraps and `.get()` may return a non-empty unintended slice.

title: `16 + version_len` may overflow usize on 32-bit when version_len is attacker-controlled u32
description: Untrusted u32 added to 16 without checked_add can wrap to small value, bypassing subsequent length check.

title: Small-format data_size read as single u8 but spec is u8
description: Per ECMA-335 the small section data_size IS u8 so max 255 bytes — fine, but no validation that data_size >= 4 before subtraction (saturating_sub hides malformed input as zero clauses, silently).

title: `raw: data.to_vec()` clones entire input buffer on every parse
description: Unnecessary heap allocation/copy; should borrow or accept ownership explicitly.

title: Fat EH section data_size u24 decoded with wrong byte placement
description: `u32::from_le_bytes([0, bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]])` left-shifts each byte by an extra 8 bits, yielding a value 256x too large and an inflated clause_count.

title: stream_data uses unchecked start + size for slice end
description: Attacker-controlled u32 offset+size can wrap on 32-bit targets, and there is no validation that end >= start before .get(start..end).

title: version_end = 16 + version_len uses untrusted u32 without checked_add
description: A crafted version_len near usize::MAX wraps to a small index, defeating the subsequent length check and yielding wrong parse results.

title: Small-format clause_count uses saturating_sub on data_size
description: Malformed sections with data_size < 4 are silently treated as zero clauses rather than reported as Truncated, hiding parser errors from callers.

title: CilMetadataReader::parse clones the entire input buffer into self.raw
description: Unnecessary heap copy on every parse; should borrow with a lifetime or accept Vec<u8> ownership.

title: tableswitch high-low+1 can overflow i32
description: `(high - low + 1)` is computed in i32 on attacker-controlled values and will panic in debug / wrap in release before the `.max(0)` saturates it.

title: tableswitch count arithmetic overflows i32
description: Same `(high - low + 1)` pattern; `high=i32::MAX, low<0` overflows before clamp, and `count * 4` can also overflow usize on 32-bit hosts leading to undersized `need` check.

title: get_branches mis-reads goto_w/jsr_w/switch targets
description: All branch/call instrs are decoded as i16 from bytes[1..3], but goto_w/jsr_w carry a 4-byte offset and tableswitch/lookupswitch have no such field — branch target is wrong.

title: MemoryRegion::contains can overflow
description: base + size is unchecked u64 addition; a region near u64::MAX wraps and contains() returns wrong results.

title: MemoryInspector::read addr+size unchecked
description: addr + size as u64 and base + data.len() as u64 can wrap silently, allowing a read past mapped end to spuriously succeed or fail.

title: read_u64_le unwraps try_into
description: If read returns fewer than 8 bytes (shouldn't, but no invariant enforced), try_into().unwrap() panics in library code.

title: MockDebugger::read_memory silently truncates
description: end = (offset+size).min(page.len()) returns fewer bytes than requested with no error, breaking the read_memory contract.

title: MockDebugger::write_memory is a no-op that reports success
description: Ignores addr/data entirely and returns Ok(data.len()), producing false-positive writes that mask test bugs.

title: DebugEvent timestamp truncates u128 nanos to u64
description: d.as_nanos() as u64 silently truncates; safe until ~2554 but the `as` cast hides overflow and there's no #[allow] or comment.

title: Binary memory write payload corrupted by UTF-8 lossy conversion
description: `write_binary_cmd` runs escaped raw bytes through `String::from_utf8_lossy`, replacing any non-UTF8 byte (most bytes >0x7F) with U+FFFD, so the `X` packet transmits wrong data to the target.

title: is_connected defaults to true on lock contention
description: `try_lock().map(...).unwrap_or(true)` reports a disconnected/contended debugger as connected, leading callers to issue commands that will fail.

title: step_over PC+5 can wrap u64
description: `pc + 5` on a u64 PC near address-space end overflows in debug builds (panic) and wraps silently in release, planting a breakpoint at address 0.

title: Backtrace fp+16 can wrap u64
description: `sp = fp + 16` during frame-pointer unwind has no checked_add; a corrupt or attacker-controlled saved rbp causes panic/wrap.

title: memory-map qXfer length capped at 0xfff bytes
description: Requesting only 4095 bytes of the memory-map XML silently truncates the map for any non-trivial target, returning a partial/empty `Vec<MemoryMap>`.

title: All-0xFF register chunk misidentified as "unavailable"
description: Real registers with legitimate value 0xFFFF... (e.g. -1 sentinels, MXCSR masks) are dropped from the RegisterSet because the unavailable marker is `xx` (not 0xff bytes) per GDB spec.

title: return_status overlaps processor field
description: return_status is parsed from bytes [4..8] which reuses bytes 4-5 already used for `processor`, instead of bytes [4..8] non-overlapping (should likely be data[8..12] or padding); wrong field decoding.

title: from_bytes panics on truncated packet
description: `raw[HEADER_SIZE..HEADER_SIZE + byte_count]` slices without verifying raw.len() >= that range, causing a panic on a short/malformed packet from an attacker-controlled transport.

title: byte_count truncates data.len() to u16
description: `data.len() as u16` silently wraps when payload exceeds 65535 bytes, producing a malformed packet with mismatched length.

title: parse_recv re-parses already-consumed bytes after short packet
description: when from_bytes succeeds but recv_buf has fewer than `total` bytes the loop breaks without consuming, yet next iteration re-decodes the same header repeatedly; also `from_bytes` returns Some even when payload bytes are missing (out-of-bounds risk via line 250 panic).

title: O(n) remove(0) on malformed stream
description: on unknown packet type, `recv_buf.remove(0)` is O(n); a stream of garbage bytes causes quadratic CPU usage.

title: Unchecked address+size in map overlap check
description: `address + size` and `r.address + r.size` can wrap u64 and bypass overlap detection, allowing aliased regions.

title: Unbounded allocation from caller-controlled size
description: `vec![0u8; size as usize]` panics or OOMs when callers pass huge sizes, and `size as usize` truncates on 32-bit hosts.

title: read() silently zero-pads past region end
description: Reading more than region size returns zero-padded buffer instead of an error, masking out-of-bounds reads.

title: VmRegionInfo::end() overflows on high addresses
description: `self.address + self.size` is unchecked u64 addition; a region near u64::MAX overflows and makes `contains` wrongly return false.

title: cpsr truncated via `as u32` without check
description: `Arm64ThreadState::from_array` silently drops the upper 32 bits of element 33 when constructing cpsr.

title: page_align overflows on large values
description: value + page_size-1 wraps to 0 for inputs near u64::MAX, producing wrong alignment.

title: add_section size arithmetic can underflow/overflow
description: section.address - addr + section.size has no checked arithmetic and panics or wraps on crafted inputs.

title: read_memory bounds check overflows
description: addr + size as u64 can wrap past u64::MAX, bypassing the end check and slicing out-of-bounds (panic).

title: Passes that change length are silently dropped
description: The `if result.len() == current.len()` guard discards any pass whose output differs in length, never applying real deobfuscation that adds/removes bytes.

title: Perturbation resets no_progress before retrying
description: Setting `no_progress_count = 0` immediately after perturbing means the loop cannot detect that perturbation also failed and will keep perturbing forever in pathological cases.

title: partial_cmp().unwrap() panics on NaN quality_delta
description: `rank_perturbations` will panic if any `quality_delta` is NaN (e.g. from log2(0) edge cases in entropy), use `total_cmp` instead.

title: Hash-constant heuristic ignores endianness
description: `u32::from_le_bytes` is hardcoded to little-endian; big-endian binaries will have their hash constants completely missed by the IADL detector.

title: partial_cmp unwrap panics on NaN scores
description: select_best uses partial_cmp(..).unwrap() which panics if any combined_score is NaN, and the same pattern recurs at line 1943.

title: Negative jump target cast to usize wraps
description: `(end as i64 + 2 + i64::from(rel)) as usize` for a negative backward branch produces a huge usize with no bounds validation before returning as a CFG successor (also at line 706).

title: step_by(0) panics when window_size is 1
description: `step_by(self.window_size / 2)` panics when window_size==1 since step_by requires non-zero step, and the constructor does not validate window_size.

title: offset+length addition may overflow usize
description: `planned.offset + planned.length` is computed before the bounds check, so a malicious/garbage plan triggers a debug-mode overflow panic; should use saturating_add like the PatchApplicator does.

title: enumerate_values has no combinatorial cap
description: Doc claims sample_count cap but function unconditionally generates range^n entries causing OOM/DoS for >=3 variables at default bits=8 (16M+ HashMaps).

title: Signed test domain never reaches negative values
description: Comment promises sign-extension but `indices[i] as i64` of a small u64 yields only non-negative values, so opaque predicates relying on negative inputs (e.g. signed comparisons) are misclassified.

title: bits.min(16) silently truncates configured width
description: TruthTableChecker.bits is u32 but enumeration silently caps at 16 with no error/warning, so callers configuring 32-bit domains test a tiny subset and may report AlwaysTrue for predicates false at larger values.

title: Shl/Shr accepts u8 shift but wrapping_shl masks to 6 bits
description: OpaqueExpr::Shl(_, n: u8) allows n>=64, then wrapping_shl(n as u32) silently masks the shift count, diverging from real machine semantics and causing wrong classification of shift-based predicates.

title: classify returns Unknown when all assignments evaluate to None
description: After the loop, `(false,false)` (all div-by-zero) returns Unknown but earlier in-loop early-return on None makes this dead; also if vars empty and is_const None, returns Unknown — inconsistent with Unknown vs unevaluable semantics.

title: wrapping_abs of i64::MIN yields i64::MIN
description: Abs evaluator uses wrapping_abs so Abs(i64::MIN)==i64::MIN, breaking the abs(x)>=0 invariant (Pattern 21) when that input appears, producing incorrect AlwaysTrue classification.

title: XOR-loop region size derived from wrong byte
description: `end = dest_addr + u64::from(key)` where `key = data[i+1]` is the low byte of the imm32 counter, not the loop count, producing incorrect region lengths.

title: Rol/Ror algorithm dispatch swapped
description: `SmcAlgorithm::Rol` invokes `ror8` and `SmcAlgorithm::Ror` invokes `rol8`, contradicting the documented semantics on lines 46-49.

title: extract_key_from_block mask is wrong
description: `block[i+1] & 0x30 == 0x30` matches many non-XOR ModR/M bytes; the XOR opcode-extension nibble check should use `& 0x38 == 0x30` like `trace()` does.

title: ADD-loop opcode mask too loose
description: `data[i+1] & 0xF8 == 0x00` matches ModR/M bytes 0x00-0x07 used by many `80 /reg` forms (including XOR, OR), causing false ADD detections.

title: Negative jump cast wraps to huge usize
description: `(pc as i64 + 2 + offset) as usize` with a negative result wraps to ~`usize::MAX`, relying on the loop condition rather than a safe checked conversion.

title: reconstruct() can overflow base_addr+i
description: `base_addr + i as u64` is unchecked; a near-`u64::MAX` `base_addr` plus index wraps silently and produces wrong map lookups.

title: ADD-loop ModR/M mask too loose
description: `data[i+1] & 0xF8 == 0x00` accepts ModR/M bytes 0x00-0x07 shared by other `80 /reg` opcodes, causing false ADD region detections.

title: SpecEventLogger::spawn panics if called twice
description: `.expect("SpecEventLogger::spawn called more than once")` panics in library code instead of returning a Result.

title: RwLock unwrap will panic on poison
description: Every `.unwrap()` on std `RwLock`/`Mutex` (lines 580,588,597,607,621,668,670,679,684,690,694,728,730,769,770,853,862,894,900,910,911,938,941,969) propagates panics from any poisoned lock, taking down unrelated subsystems.

title: event_count linear scan instead of HashMap lookup
description: `event_count` iterates the entire counters map with `.find` instead of `.get(variant_name)`, O(n) per call and unnecessary.

title: RingBuf::new panics on huge capacity
description: `capacity.next_power_of_two()` panics if `capacity > usize::MAX/2 + 1`, an unchecked input from public `new`.

title: Magic-bytes comparison wrong length
description: `data[0..4] == b"IDASGN"` compares 4 vs 6 bytes, always false, so v6+ files only detected via legacy 0x54/0x4A path.

title: Header length check off-by-two
description: Check is `< offset + 26` but code reads `data[offset+27]` at line 546 and slices `..offset+27` at 544, panicking on minimally-sized inputs.

title: Silent CRC truncation accepts short buffers
description: `crc_end = (crc_start + crc_length).min(data.len())` computes CRC over a shortened range, then compares against expected CRC of full length — can produce false matches or incorrect rejections instead of failing cleanly.

title: Unchecked addition of attacker-controlled lengths
description: `crc_start + pat.crc_length as usize` can overflow on 32-bit hosts when `pat.crc_length` (u16) plus offset is crafted via deserialized data; should use `checked_add`.

title: `partial_cmp().unwrap()` on f64 confidence
description: If a NaN sneaks into `confidence.combined` (e.g. from division), the sort comparator panics in library code.

title: Wrong CRC polynomial vs lib.rs crc16_flirt
description: This module's crc16_flirt uses poly 0xA001 (CRC-16-ARC) while lib.rs uses 0x8408 (true FLIRT poly), so apply_engine will reject every valid FLIRT pattern's CRC.

title: Inconsistent CRC region offset calculation
description: apply_engine computes `crc_off = fn_offset + crc_offset` while lib.rs uses `fn_offset + pat_len + crc_offset`, so the two engines hash different bytes for the same signature.

title: CRC check silently skipped when buffer too short
description: When `crc_end > data.len()` the CRC verification is skipped instead of treated as failure, allowing unverified matches near buffer end (also at lines 508, 561, 1354, 1392).

title: expect() in public library function build_ac_index
description: Public API panics on builder error instead of returning Result, propagating panics into callers.

title: Unchecked mask/bytes length mismatch in WildcardPattern::from_signature
description: Indexes `sig.mask[i]` without verifying `mask.len() == bytes.len()`, panicking on user-constructed FlirtSignature with mismatched vectors.

title: compute_favorites uses coverage_bits as bit-index proxy
description: `favored_bits[bits_count]` indexes by hit count rather than which bits are covered, so set-cover is meaningless and most entries with same coverage_bits are not favored.

title: next_usize truncates u64 to usize on 32-bit before modulo
description: `(self.next_u64() as usize) % n` on 32-bit platforms discards high bits, biasing distribution and making `next_usize` non-uniform for large n.

title: ForkServer.next_pid increments without wrap check
description: `self.next_pid += 1` will panic in debug on overflow after long runs; should use wrapping_add or u64.

title: select_sequential asserts non-empty queue
description: Library API panics rather than returning Result/Option, easy to trip from outside callers.

title: Dictionary load_afl_format mishandles quoted strings with escapes
description: Inner `&line[1..line.len()-1]` is taken as raw bytes; AFL dict format supports `\xNN` escapes which are silently kept literal, producing incorrect tokens.

title: AflQueue.next_id increments without overflow check
description: `self.next_id += 1` panics in debug on u64 wrap; trivially unreachable but still an unchecked arithmetic op flagged by lints.

title: Wrong nth() index parsing BB count
description: `line.split_whitespace().nth(2)` returns "bbs" not the count N for "BB Table: N bbs", so bb_count is parsed from the wrong token and silently becomes 0.

title: Inconsistent DRcov BB on-disk layout vs V2 parser
description: DrcovFile::parse reads `[module_id u16][start u32][size u16]` while DrcovBasicBlock::parse_bb_table (and the documented spec at L1297) reads `[start u32][size u16][module_id u16]`, so the two parsers decode the same bytes into completely different fields.

title: CRLF breaks DrcovHeader byte-offset accounting
description: `consumed += version_line.len() + 1` assumes a single '\n' terminator, but `str::lines()` also strips '\r\n'; on CRLF files the returned `hdr_consumed` is short by one byte per line, corrupting downstream slicing.

title: locate_binary_start misses last position
description: The loop bound `data.len().saturating_sub(marker_bytes.len())` is exclusive, so a marker placed at the very last possible offset is not found.

title: absolute_addr can wrap on high module bases
description: `module_base + u64::from(self.start)` performs unchecked addition; with adversarial input near `u64::MAX` it silently wraps.

title: SRA modelled as logical Shr
description: Z80 SRA (arithmetic right shift) preserves sign bit but the lifter emits IrExpr::Shr (logical), losing the sign-extension semantics.

title: ROR CF when count==0 reads wrong bit
description: The `("cf","ror")` branch has no n==0 guard, so a zero count returns bit(v, w-1) instead of leaving CF unchanged, contradicting Intel SDM.

title: Byte slice on potentially non-ASCII mnemonic
description: `&without_s[without_s.len()-2..]` will panic if the mnemonic contains a multibyte UTF-8 char at the boundary.

title: Silent `as u8` truncation of align
description: `parse_u64(v).unwrap_or(0) as u8` silently truncates align values >255 to a wrong low byte instead of erroring.

title: Unwrap after match guard is redundant but fragile
description: `operand_list.first().unwrap()` after a `Some(Operand::Memory{..})` match relies on pattern guarantees; harmless today but a refactor that adds an `if`-guard would turn this into a panic in lib code.

title: Rol/Ror shift-by-bit-width panic
description: When eval_expr(r) % bits == 0, `lv >> (bits - shift)` shifts by full bit-width which is undefined-behavior shift and panics in debug.

title: Memory read addr+i can overflow u64
description: read() computes `addr + i as u64` without wrapping/checked add, panicking on near-u64::MAX addresses in debug builds.

title: BlockBuilder.end set to start address
description: `build()` sets `end = Address::new(self.start)` ignoring instruction extents, so block end is always equal to start and downstream range checks will be wrong.

title: Dominance-frontier walks through u32::MAX
description: If `idom[&b.id]` stays `u32::MAX` (unreachable block) the `while runner != idom[&b.id]` loop indexes `idom[&u32::MAX]` and panics or never terminates.

title: Shl/Shr ignore operand Size
description: Constant folding shifts a full u64 and does not truncate to the declared `Size`, producing wrong constants for Byte/Word/DWord operands.

title: Const-fold Shl masks shift by 63 regardless of Size
description: `a << (b & 63)` can shift past the operand width for 32/16/8-bit sizes and never truncates the result, yielding incorrect folded constants.

title: elf_arch_hint OOB index
description: checks bytes.len() < 19 then indexes bytes[19], panicking when input length is exactly 19.

title: ext2 magic check off-by-one
description: guard bytes.len() >= 1080 still indexes bytes[1081], panicking for inputs of length 1080 or 1081.

title: unchecked base+offset add
description: `base + reloc.offset_in_image` can overflow u64 and panic in debug builds for attacker-controlled offsets.

title: MipsHi16 unchecked add
description: `full + 0x8000` is a plain u64 add that panics in debug when full is near u64::MAX after wrapping_add_signed.

title: unchecked file_offset+delta
description: `self.file_offset + delta` can overflow u64 for crafted segment metadata, panicking in debug builds.

title: GnuHashTable::lookup panics when nbuckets is 0
description: `hash % self.nbuckets` panics if a malformed .gnu.hash section has nbuckets=0 (no validation in parse64).

title: GnuBloomFilter::might_contain panics if word_bits is 0
description: `self.word_bits - 1` underflows and `hash / self.word_bits` divides by zero; constructor accepts any u32.

title: get_section_name_table can overflow on 32-bit usize
description: `off + sz` adds two attacker-controlled section header fields without checked_add, can wrap and cause a panic on slicing.

title: Shdr32/64::parse_all overflows on attacker-controlled e_shoff/e_shnum
description: `e_shoff as usize + i * step` is unchecked; on 32-bit usize a large e_shoff and big e_shnum wrap silently, producing wrong parses.

title: PatchBytesTool offset+patch.len() can overflow usize
description: attacker-supplied `offset` (u64) is cast to usize then added to patch.len() without checked_add, causing wraparound and a subsequent out-of-bounds slice write or false bounds-check pass on 32-bit targets.

title: SectionDumpTool off+len wraps before bounds check
description: `off + len` (both user-controlled u64s cast to usize) can overflow, making `end > d.len()` falsely return false and panicking on slice or returning wrong region.

title: HexDumpTool off+len overflow before .min()
description: `off + len` is computed before `.min(data.len())`, so a large user `offset` plus default `len = data.len()` overflows usize and triggers undefined truncation/panic on the slice.

title: XorDecryptTool silently truncates 64-bit key to u8
description: `k as u8` drops high bits of the user-supplied `key` (u64) with no validation, so callers passing 0x100 get XOR with 0x00 instead of an error.

title: demangle_simple slices &s[..n] on UTF-8 boundaries
description: the parsed length `n` is treated as a byte offset but `s` may contain non-ASCII bytes, so `&s[..n]` panics on a non-char-boundary input rather than returning the original name.

title: base64_decode silently drops trailing partial chunks
description: chunks shorter than 4 are skipped with `break`, so malformed or unpadded base64 inputs return a truncated result instead of an error.

title: BMH skip table unsound for masked pattern bytes
description: skip table only records the literal `value` byte, leaving other bytes that satisfy the mask with the default full-length skip, causing valid matches to be skipped.

title: Unchecked u64 address+offset arithmetic in read/write
description: `addr.0 + i` and `addr.0 + i as u64` can wrap on near-u64::MAX addresses, silently aliasing reads/writes to low addresses in release builds.

title: `span()` panics or wraps when max key is u64::MAX
description: `Address::new(max + 1)` overflows when the largest stored byte is at u64::MAX, panicking in debug and wrapping to 0 in release.

title: Offset cast u64 to usize loses bits on 32-bit targets
description: `(addr - base) as usize` silently truncates large offsets on 32-bit builds, allowing out-of-bounds reads/writes to pass the subsequent bounds check.

title: Indexing assumes provider returned exact length
description: `bytes[0]` (and similar in u16/u32/u64 readers) will panic if a custom `MemoryProvider` returns a shorter `Vec` than requested, instead of returning `None`.

title: `current += bytes_this_page` can wrap u64 near address space end
description: Reads/writes spanning the top of the 64-bit address space wrap `current` to 0, causing an infinite loop or wrong-page lookups.

title: V2 PAGE_USE_EXTRA uses page_idx as extras index
description: Comment admits heuristic: use page_idx as index - correct dyld semantics require the extras index from the page_starts value masked, not page_idx, producing wrong/missing fixups.

title: V2 apply omits value_add when rebuilding pointer
description: Computes `(raw & value_mask) + slide` but ignores `v2.value_add`, so rebased pointers are off by value_add.

title: V2 EXTRA_END loop continuation inverted
description: Loop continues while `e & EXTRA_END == 0` is false; per dyld, `EXTRA_END` set means this is the LAST entry, so the loop should break when set.

title: V2 chain stride uses *4 for 64-bit pointers
description: `ptr_off += delta as usize * 4` - V2 uses 8-byte pointers, value_mask combined with line 492 yields wrong chain walking.

title: va_to_file_offset uses non-saturating add
description: `self.file_offset + (va - self.address)` can overflow if file_offset+size exceeds u64.

title: read_at_va integer overflow in slice index
description: `data.get(file_off..file_off + len)` can overflow usize for attacker-controlled `len`.

title: Fmt22x truncates 16-bit register vBBBB to 8 bits
description: format 22x stores BBBB as u8::try_from(word(1) & 0xff), mis-mapping register index >= 256.

title: Fmt32x truncates 16-bit registers vAAAA/vBBBB to 8 bits
description: both 16-bit register operands in 32x are masked with & 0xff and pushed as u8.

title: Fmt3rc register-range computation can panic on overflow
description: (cccc + u16::from(i)) & 0xff performs u16 addition that panics in debug.

title: fill-array-data size can overflow usize on 32-bit
description: num_elem * elem_width is unchecked usize multiplication of attacker-controlled DEX payload fields.

title: descriptor_to_type panics on multibyte UTF-8 after '['
description: &d[1..] slices a &str at byte 1; multibyte char causes panic.

title: block_at_offset misses bytes within the last instruction of a block
description: end is set to the start offset of the last instruction (not its end).

title: Windows QMP transport mismatch
description: resolve_qmp_socket returns filesystem .sock path but Windows QmpClient::connect expects tcp: prefix.

title: wait_for_qmp_ready ignores QEMU exit
description: Poll loop only checks socket exists.

title: revert is a no-op
description: State set Reverting then immediately Stopped.

title: delete_snapshot orphans children
description: No re-parenting.

title: Unbounded event loop in send_command
description: Skips event lines forever.

title: JSON array split on raw comma breaks nested objects/strings
description: split(',') splits inside strings/nested.

title: JSON object parser is a silent stub
description: Returns empty Map.

title: JSON string serialization escapes only quote
description: Does not escape backslash/controls/newlines.

title: base64_decode silently accepts truncated input
description: Residual cnt==1 ignored.

title: pattern_find_all missing empty-pattern guard
description: Empty pattern produces len+1 matches.

title: glob_match has exponential backtracking
description: Naive recursion on *.

title: Unrestricted file read in store_load_binary
description: No sandboxing.

title: i64::MIN % -1 panics
description: Overflows.

title: Unchecked start+len in get_bytes
description: Wrap on 32-bit usize.

title: Pow exponent truncated to i32
description: b as i32 truncates.

title: is_complete true for zero-total progress
description: 0>=0 true.

title: Segment::empty start_ea + size can overflow u64
description: No saturating add.

title: vec[0u8; size as usize] truncates u64 size on 32-bit
description: OOM on 64-bit.

title: read_word/read_dword/read_qword add without overflow check
description: ea+1 overflow.

title: read_u32_le/read_u64_le panic on short buffers
description: expect on bounds.

title: patch_bytes bound check can overflow usize
description: Use checked_add.

title: UTF-16 string scanner truncates surrogate-pair code units silently
description: Drops surrogate halves.

title: Symbol id lookup uses last underscore segment
description: rsplit('_').next parses only suffix.

title: alias_check end-address can overflow u64
description: a + size_a wraps.

title: as_u32_le accepts >4 bytes and silently truncates
description: Delegates to u64.

title: Out-of-bounds index when arg_count exceeds args length
description: If `entry.arg_count as usize` exceeds `entry.args.len()` the indexing `entry.args[i]` panics in library code.

title: Unary negation overflow on i64::MIN retval
description: `(-retval) as u32` overflows when retval is i64::MIN, panicking in debug and wrapping silently in release.

title: Same i64::MIN negation overflow in SyscallExit::errno
description: `Some((-self.retval) as u32)` is UB-prone for i64::MIN, panics in debug builds.

title: ChildTracker::len()/is_empty broken
description: `children_of.len() + 1` always returns >=1 so `is_empty()` returns false even for an empty tracker.

title: NumberRange does not validate lo<=hi
description: `NumberRange { lo, hi }` with lo>hi silently never matches, hiding caller bugs.

title: Duplicate SSN 0x55 for NtCreateFile collides with NtCreateTimer
description: NtCreateFile is inserted with SSN 0x55 but NtCreateTimer already owns 0x55, so by_ssn(0x55) returns NtCreateFile and NtCreateTimer is lost from the table.

title: NTSTATUS success check uses wrong bit shift
description: `s >> 30 == 0` treats warning/informational statuses (0x4000_xxxx, 0x8000_xxxx) as failures; per NTSTATUS spec only the top bit (>> 31) distinguishes success from error.

title: next_seq can panic on overflow in debug or wrap silently
description: `self.next_seq += 1` lacks checked/saturating handling, and the same pattern in api_monitor/windows_events means a long-running interceptor can wrap seq numbers and corrupt on_return lookups.

title: ApiHookRule.matches is case-sensitive on function despite doc claim
description: Doc string says "case-insensitive" and dll uses eq_ignore_ascii_case, but function uses `==`, so a rule for "NtCreateFile" won't match "ntcreatefile" contrary to documented behavior.

title: EventProviderGuid Display emits non-standard GUID format
description: Format `{XXXXXXXX-XXXXXXXX-XXXXXXXX-XXXXXXXX}` uses four 8-hex groups instead of the canonical 8-4-4-4-12 layout, producing strings that no Windows GUID parser will accept.

title: SysEnterPattern.matches accepts trailing bytes silently
description: `actual.len() < self.bytes.len()` rejects only short inputs; longer inputs match on prefix only, which may produce false positives when callers expect exact-length matching.

title: Unbounded recursion in `attach_children` self-cycle
description: If a `ProcessInfo` has `ppid == pid`, parent_map maps the pid to itself causing infinite recursion and stack overflow.

title: `walk_dir` follows symlinks with no loop or symlink-cycle protection
description: `std::fs::read_dir` follows symlinks, so a symlinked directory cycle causes unbounded recursion and stack overflow.

title: `content_contains` reads entire file into memory
description: Reading arbitrarily large files via `std::fs::read` during walk enables OOM/DoS when scanning directories with huge files.

title: PE `pe_offset + 4 > data.len()` can overflow on attacker-controlled input
description: `pe_offset` is a `u32` from file bytes cast to usize; `pe_offset + 4` and later `opt_offset + 0x88` can wrap on 32-bit and bypass bounds checks; use checked_add.

title: Glob matcher has exponential backtracking
description: `glob_match_inner` on patterns like `*a*a*a*a*b` against long inputs causes exponential time (ReDoS-like) since it tries both branches without memoization.

title: parent_domain mishandles multi-label TLDs
description: For "foo.example.co.uk" returns "co.uk", causing false-positive eTLD+1 matches across unrelated domains.

title: ip_prefix_24 accepts non-numeric octets
description: `split('.')` of arbitrary string passes len==4 check, so "a.b.c.d" produces "a.b.c" prefix, polluting correlation evidence.

title: Temporal overlap reports 1 day even when windows don't actually intersect
description: When only the tolerance-expanded windows touch, `overlap_end < overlap_start`; saturating_sub yields 0 then +1, fabricating a 1-day "overlap".

title: Clamp on `similarity_threshold` is ineffective because field is `pub`
description: Constructor clamps to [0,1] but the field can be set directly to any f64, defeating the invariant relied on by the clusterer.

title: MispRawClient sends API key over plaintext TCP for https URLs
description: parse_host_port strips `https://` then connects with raw TcpStream and no TLS, leaking the Authorization header on the wire for any https base_url.

title: parse_host_port misparses URLs containing a path
description: `rsplit_once(':')` and the lack of path stripping treat `host/path` or `host:port/path` as host, producing wrong TCP target and a port parse failure that silently defaults to 443.

title: STIX pattern built by unescaped string interpolation
description: attr.value is inserted directly into single-quoted STIX patterns, so any value containing `'` breaks the pattern or allows STIX-pattern injection in downstream consumers.

title: event.id (u64) cast to i64 wraps for ids > i64::MAX
description: `event.id.unwrap_or(0) as i64` and `id as i64` in get_by_id silently wrap large MISP event IDs to negative values, corrupting cache lookups.

title: read_response uses from_utf8_lossy on HTTP body
description: JSON bytes containing invalid UTF-8 (or any binary) get replaced with U+FFFD before parsing, silently corrupting responses instead of erroring.

title: Nonce-counter wraparound check happens after use
description: fetch_add returns prior value so ctr==u32::MAX is checked after that nonce was already emitted, and the next call reuses counter 0 with the same salt, breaking ChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce-uniqueness.

title: PerfEventCounter::read ignores short reads
description: read(2) may return 0<n<8 yet the code returns the partially-initialized u64 as the counter value, producing wrong instruction counts.

title: read_memory can fault past requested length
description: the PEEKDATA loop always reads a full word even when only a few trailing bytes are needed, so when addr+len sits just before an unmapped page the syscall faults and aborts a valid read.

title: Checkpoint counter silently saturates
description: position_counter uses saturating_add(1), so after u64::MAX checkpoints every further checkpoint collides on the same TtdPosition instead of erroring.

title: Nanosecond timestamp truncated to u64
description: `d.as_nanos() as u64` truncates the u128, narrowing salt entropy and making salt collisions more likely between concurrent encryptors built from the same key.

title: Output path built by string concatenation
description: `format!("{}/trace_{}.run", output_dir, n)` ignores trailing separators and never validates output_dir, allowing path-traversal-style names from caller-controlled config.

title: RunFileHeader::SIZE=72 but doc says 64 and parser only reads 64 bytes
description: Constant claims 72 bytes while only fields up through offset 64 are read/written, causing 8-byte misalignment when parser advances `pos` and subsequent reads land in the wrong place.

title: SequenceId::next can panic on overflow
description: `self.0 + 1` is unchecked and will panic in debug builds when sequence reaches u64::MAX; should use `wrapping_add` or `checked_add`.

title: mark_writes loses prior dirty bits and mishandles lower base
description: The condition `base_page > min_page || n_pages < new` rebuilds bitmap from scratch, discarding previously marked dirty pages, and if old base was below min_page it silently keeps the old (potentially smaller) bitmap missing new high pages.

title: mark_writes computes end_page with unchecked add
description: `addr + data.len() as u64` can overflow when an attacker-controlled write address is near u64::MAX, panicking in debug builds.

title: bytes_added not counted for new zero-filled pages
description: Added pages whose content equals the all-zero `empty` placeholder fail the `b_page != a_page` check, so they are silently dropped from the diff and byte counters.

title: Inner doc comments after items
description: `//!` doc comments at lines 16-22 appear after `pub mod` items, which is invalid Rust (inner attributes must precede all items) and will fail to compile.

title: Premature break assumes sorted events
description: `find_last_write_before` breaks on first `ev_tick >= tick` assuming events are tick-ordered, but `push_event` appends without sorting the events vec, so later writes with smaller ticks are missed.

title: Same unsorted-events break in find_last_write_range_before
description: Identical early-break bug: events vec is not enforced sorted by tick, so the function can return a stale "last" write.

title: Unnecessary clone of entire event
description: `apply_event_forward` clones the whole `TraceEvent` (including all mem_writes Vec<u8>) just to satisfy the borrow checker, causing O(N) allocation per forward step on large traces.

title: StringCount condition ignores count value
description: `Condition::StringCount(id)` returns `len() > 0`, identical to `StringMatch`, so any rule using `#id == N` semantics is broken.

title: parse_string_value panics on short/non-ASCII text
description: `raw.find('"').unwrap_or(raw.len()-1) + 1` underflows when raw is empty and slices on non-char boundaries when the value contains multibyte UTF-8, causing a panic in library code.

title: Condition parser has inverted operator precedence
description: `parse_condition_text` checks ` and ` before ` or ` via `splitn`, ignoring left-to-right precedence and parenthesisation, producing wrong boolean trees for non-trivial conditions.

title: Recursive directory walk follows symlinks
description: `walk_dir_for_rules` and `walk_scan` recurse on `path.is_dir()` without checking symlinks, allowing infinite loops or path traversal out of the intended tree.

title: scan_directory loads every file fully into RAM
description: `walk_scan` calls `std::fs::read(&path)` on every regular file with no size cap, so a single large file in a scanned tree exhausts memory.

title: partial_cmp().unwrap() panics on NaN confidence
description: Sorting/`max_by` on `Confidence` floats unwraps `partial_cmp`, which returns None for NaN and panics in library code.

title: top_hypothesis panics on NaN confidence
description: Same NaN-unwrap pattern in `max_by`; a single NaN-valued hypothesis crashes the reasoning engine.

title: usize→u32 token estimate truncates on large histories
description: `(chars / 4) as u32` silently wraps when summed message content exceeds ~16 GiB/4, producing wrong token estimates that may bypass limits.

title: Relative jump-table target computation truncates high addresses
description: Casting `base_addr as i64` truncates u64 addresses above i64::MAX (e.g. kernel-space) before adding the rel32, producing wrong targets.

title: code_base + offset can wrap on high bases
description: `base + i as u64 + 5` and `next_ip.wrapping_add_signed` silently wrap when `code_base` is near u64::MAX, producing bogus xref source/target addresses without diagnostics.

title: Linear scan re-decodes displacement bytes as opcodes
description: `extract_code_to_code` always advances `i += 1` even after matching a 5-byte E8/E9, so disp32 bytes (which can legally be 0xE8/0xE9) generate spurious phantom call/jump xrefs.

title: Abstract virtual detection only flags null slots
description: `is_abstract: fn_addr == 0` misses MSVC `_purecall`/Itanium `__cxa_pure_virtual` stubs whose addresses are non-zero, mislabelling pure virtuals as concrete.

title: is_likely_tail_call accepts sites past function end
description: The check is `site <= function_end` with no lower bound and no membership test against the function's range, so any JMP anywhere below `function_end` to a known function is flagged as a tail call.

title: apply_fixups subtracts base from fixup.offset without bounds check
description: If fixup.offset < base this panics in debug or wraps to huge usize in release silently dropping fixups.

title: Default analyze_call_site caps register args at 4
description: `.min(4)` clamps reg-arg count even for SysV (6 regs) / AAPCS64 (8 regs), producing wrong call-site analysis.

title: AAPCS32 float arg name is literal "sN" instead of actual register
description: Returned ArgLocation always has name "sN" instead of "s0".."s15", breaking downstream consumers that key on register name.

title: aapcs64_ninth_arg_is_stack uses bare matches! without assert
description: `matches!(...)` returns bool that is discarded, so the test never actually verifies the location is on the stack.

title: PE lfanew bounds check `lfanew + 6 <= buf.len()` can overflow on 32-bit
description: Untrusted u32 lfanew cast to usize then added to 6 can wrap on 32-bit targets, bypassing the bound check and panicking on the subsequent slice.

title: Mach-O probe unwraps buf[0..4].try_into() with only a 4-byte minimum
description: Reachable code path; if some earlier change relaxes the len<4 guard, the unwrap panics—use unwrap_or like the sibling lines for consistency/defense-in-depth.

title: SBC binary mode underflows u16 in debug
description: `state.a as u16 - v as u16 - borrow` panics in debug builds whenever a < v+borrow (the common borrow case), corrupting all SBC semantics.

title: ADC BCD overflow flag computed from wrong bin_result
description: `a ^ bin_result as u8` truncates the 9-bit `bin_result` before XOR, so the V flag is wrong whenever the binary sum produces carry, mis-detecting signed overflow.

title: Direct-page address adds 8-bit Const8 instead of widening
description: `E::add(E::reg(IL_REG_D), E::Const8(op1))` treats op1 as 8-bit, but 65816 direct-page math is 16-bit; downstream analysis sees a truncated operand.

title: Branch target cast next_pc as i16 wraps for high PCs
description: Casting u16 next_pc to i16 then adding offset overflows for PC>=0x8000 in debug and produces wrong targets in release; should use i32 like the 65816 branch path.

title: BRL ignores program bank when computing target
description: next_addr is a u64 that includes bank bits, but the result is masked to 24 bits and stored without preserving PBR semantics, giving wrong long-branch destinations across banks.

title: ADC BCD overflow flag XORs truncated bin_result
description: `a ^ bin_result as u8` truncates the 9-bit sum to 8 bits before the V-flag XOR, so overflow is mis-detected whenever the binary add carried out of bit 7.

title: IndirectY zero-page high byte read without page wrap
description: `E::mem16(E::Const8(op1))` issues a 16-bit load, but on 6502 the high byte must wrap inside zero page (op1+1 mod 256); the IL model loses that wrap and downstream emulation gets wrong addresses.

title: FBcc target computed without including high displacement word
description: Only ext[2..4] is used so 32-bit FBcc displacements lose their upper 16 bits, breaking far branches.

title: EA mode 6 brief extension index register field uses 3 bits instead of 4
description: `(brief >> 4) & 7` masks off the D/A selector's neighbor and misidentifies register numbers >=8 on 68020 full-format extensions.

title: EXT mask 0xFEB8 mismatches 68k encoding
description: The correct EXT mask is 0xFFB8/0x4880; the looser 0xFEB8 will match unrelated opcodes like ADDA/SUBA with similar patterns and mis-decode them as EXT.

title: extract_hex_target misparses conditional branch operands
description: trim_start_matches('$') skips nothing when operands start with cond like "C,$1234" and take_while hex-digit will consume the 'C' (a valid hex digit) returning 0xC instead of the real target, so JR C / JP C / CALL C call_targets and branch_targets are wrong.

title: opcode_cycles default arm returns 4 for prefix opcodes
description: CB/DD/ED/FD (0xCB,0xDD,0xED,0xFD) fall through to the catch-all 4-cycle case, so total_cycles in analyze() under-counts every prefixed instruction by a large margin.

title: Z80Memory::load can underflow on empty bytes at boundary
description: when bytes is empty and start==0x10000 boundary cases or when start>end after clamping, end - start can underflow usize causing panic or wrong slice; no explicit guard that addr+len fits.

title: set_s uses bitand with literal true
description: `v & true` is a no-op masquerading as intent; harmless but indicates copy-paste error and obscures the actual sign-flag predicate.

title: length cast u64->usize truncates on 32-bit
description: `len as usize` silently truncates a user-supplied u64 length on 32-bit targets, producing a wrong scan window.

title: `f.read(&mut buf)` return value ignored, magic detected from possibly-uninitialized prefix
description: `read` may return fewer than 4 bytes; the match then uses whatever happens to be in `buf`, misdetecting format for tiny files.

title: `if let Ok(_) =` ignores the TcpStream and leaks it until drop; also racy status check
description: Using `if let Ok(_) =` instead of `.is_ok()` is a clippy lint and the open connection is dropped synchronously, but the daemon-status probe has no read handshake, so any listener (not just rustre-daemon) reports "running".

title: Unknown long flags silently become config overrides
description: `apply_long_kv` falls through to `args.overrides.insert` so a typo like `--quie=true` is silently accepted as a config key instead of being rejected as unknown.

title: Long-flag matcher accepts single-letter aliases
description: `--v`, `--V`, `--h`, `--q`, `--f`, `--c` are accepted as long flags, conflating GNU long-option convention and confusing users.

title: Tilde in default config path not expanded
description: `~/.rustre.cfg` is passed to `PathBuf::from` without `$HOME` expansion, so it only matches a literal `~` directory and never finds the user's home config.

title: `version` shorthand collides with `-v` verbose
description: positional `v` maps to `Version` while `-v` means verbose, so `rustre-cli v` prints version unexpectedly when user meant verbose toggle.

title: Unknown `--key=value` silently stored as config override
description: Typos in long flags bypass validation and inject arbitrary config keys instead of erroring, masking user mistakes.

title: Long-option parser accepts `--v`/`--h`/`--q`/`--V`/`--f`/`--c` as aliases
description: Conflates short/long flag conventions and allows ambiguous invocations.

title: Tilde not expanded in default config path search
description: `PathBuf::from("~/.rustre.cfg")` never resolves to the user's home directory, so the documented default location is unreachable.

title: Positional `v` maps to Version subcommand
description: Users typing `rustre-cli v <binary>` unexpectedly hit Version instead of getting a clear error or verbose flag.

title: Config loader allows duplicate keys silently
description: `values.insert` overwrites without warning, hiding shadowed configuration entries from the user.

title: read_patched returns zero for bytes outside patch
description: Bytes outside the patch range are filled with 0 instead of the underlying original/memory bytes, so the documented "blend" returns wrong data to callers.

title: apply_to_buf unchecked u64 add
description: buf_end = buf_base + buf.len() and p_end = p_start + len() use unchecked arithmetic; with high addresses these wrap and can skip patches or pass through the bounds guard, leading to incorrect copies or panics.

title: Memory::read wraps current_addr near u64::MAX
description: addr + read_bytes uses wrapping Address::add, so a near-MAX read can wrap to a low address that happens to lie in a segment, returning wrong bytes instead of SegmentFault.

title: align_down divides by user-supplied align
description: Although guarded by `align <= 1`, the modulo still executes for any `align` value; no panic for 0, but documented contract that any non-power-of-two yields odd results is not enforced and can mis-align addresses silently.

title: Shift overflow with Size::B16 in pretty_print
description: `1u64 << (size.bits() - 1)` becomes `1u64 << 127` which panics in debug and is UB-equivalent overflow for u64.

title: Shift overflow in apply_cast sign extension for B16
description: `1u64 << (bits - 1)` with bits=128 panics on shift-overflow when casting to a 16-byte int type.

title: MemoryProvider default reads index without length check
description: `read_u8/u16/u32/u64` index `b[0..N]` after `read_bytes` which may return a shorter Vec, causing an out-of-bounds panic in library code.

title: Parser::advance panics on empty token stream
description: `&self.tokens[self.pos]` indexes before the bounds check, so an empty token vector triggers an index-out-of-bounds panic instead of returning Eof.

title: Pointer arithmetic uses unchecked add/sub/mul
description: `lu + ru * ptr_stride` and `lu - ru * ptr_stride` are plain u64 ops with no wrapping/checked variants, panicking on overflow in debug builds for large pointers or indices.

title: Cast constant folding does not mask to target width
description: `UnOp::Cast(w)` returns `Expr::Const(c, w)` without truncating `c` to `w` bits, so `(uint8_t)0x1FF` folds to 0x1FF instead of 0xFF, producing wrong decompiled values.

title: Sub/Div/Mod/And/Or/Xor x==x simplification ignores side-effects
description: `a == b` triggers `x - x → 0`, `x / x → 1`, etc. even when `a` contains a `Load` or `Call`, silently dropping observable side-effects.

title: ExprRewriter::rewrite skips most node kinds
description: Recursion only descends into BinOp and UnOp, so rules never fire inside Call args, Load ptr, Index, Ternary, or FieldAccess subtrees.

title: print_const emits garbage hex for small negative constants
description: `(0..1000)` range excludes negatives, so e.g. `Const(-1, I32)` is printed as `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` instead of `-1` or `0xFFFFFFFF`.

title: Shift folding casts i64 count via `as u32` without range check
description: A negative or >=64 shift amount is silently masked by `wrapping_shl/shr`, hiding what should be undefined-behavior diagnostics and producing results that disagree with the original semantics.

title: Pool acquire panics on empty pool
description: `self.clients[idx]` indexes an empty Vec when pool was constructed with n=0, causing an out-of-bounds panic despite the `max(1)` guard on the modulus.

title: seq number overflow on max address
description: `address + 4` for the RETURN PCodeOpJson.seq panics in debug or wraps in release when address is near u64::MAX.

title: Dominator computation uses min instead of intersect
description: Folding predecessor dominators via `pa.min(aa)` is not the Cooper et al. intersect operation and yields incorrect idoms whenever block IDs do not correspond to RPO numbering.

title: Block end is set to addr+1 ignoring instruction size
description: `PcodeBlock::push` sets `end = machine_addr + 1` regardless of the underlying instruction width, so `end` no longer represents the exclusive end of the block in bytes.

title: padding capped at 8 bytes leaves real gaps
description: `fill_padding` clamps `pad_size` to 8 via `.min(8)`, so gaps larger than 8 bytes are only partially filled and the field layout remains invalid.

title: recompute_size overflows on negative or large offsets
description: `f.offset as usize + f.size as usize` performs unchecked add over an i64-cast-to-usize, so a negative offset or huge offset overflows usize without detection.

title: unchecked array size multiplication
description: `elem.byte_size().map(|s| s * n)` can silently overflow usize for large arrays, yielding a tiny/zero size that downstream code will trust.

title: worklist solver may miss updates
description: Phase-2 only re-checks constraints when `src == var`; new points-to facts on `dst` of a Load/Store never re-trigger their dependent constraints, so the analysis can terminate before reaching the real fixed point.

title: access_count truncation
description: `aps.len() as u32` silently truncates if more than 2^32 access patterns exist for one offset (unlikely but unchecked cast in library code).

title: MSVC empty parens underflow
description: `&base[paren_open + 1..base.len() - 1]` panics when `base.len()==0` or paren is at position 0, and slices wrong bytes when `base` does not end with `)`.

title: MSVC name backref limited to digits 0-9
description: Using `c as usize - '0' as usize` only handles indices 0-9, but MSVC uses 0-9 (correct) yet `name_backrefs.contains(&name)` plus `len<10` skips registering duplicates, producing wrong index alignment for subsequent backrefs.

title: Backref table desync on duplicates
description: Skipping push when name already present (`!contains`) breaks index correspondence with MSVC spec which requires positional registration of every name.

title: Substitution base-36 off-by-one risk
description: `usize::from_str_radix(...).unwrap_or(0) + 1` silently maps unparsable indices to subs[1], masking malformed input rather than failing.

title: Itanium args parsing breaks on nested parens
description: `rfind('(')` plus `trim_end_matches(|c| c != ')')` mishandles function-pointer args like `f(int (*)(int))`, producing wrong arg split and return type.

title: `Patch::apply` offset+len can overflow usize and bypasses bounds when original.len() > patched.len()
description: `end = self.offset + self.patched.len()` may wrap, and the original-byte check then slices `self.offset..self.offset + self.original.len()` which can panic if original is longer than patched.

title: `apply_patches` patch.offset+len arithmetic can overflow
description: same unchecked addition can wrap to a small value and slip past the `> out.len()` guard, then panic in `copy_from_slice`.

title: `build_substitution_table` does not swap, producing non-bijective table
description: setting only `table[most_freq] = assumed_plaintext` leaves another cipher byte also mapping to `assumed_plaintext`, so the result is not a valid substitution.

title: RVA section bound check can overflow u32
description: `virt_addr + sec_size` is unchecked u32 addition that wraps in release builds, allowing out-of-bounds RVAs to map to bogus offsets.

title: serialize_to_bytes discards all metadata edits
description: When raw bytes are present the function only strips the strong-name signature and returns the original PE, silently dropping every rename/patch/add modification.

title: EditTransaction::rollback does not undo table mutations
description: It only truncates the editor's modification log but leaves the already-mutated MutableTables in place, so "reversible" transactions are not reversible.

title: ChangeMethodFlags/FieldFlags truncate u32 to u16
description: The public API accepts a u32 flags value but stores `*flags as u16`, silently discarding the high 16 bits so callers cannot set e.g. ImplFlags or extended attributes.

title: Replay duration subtraction can underflow
description: `start.elapsed().as_micros() as u64 - self.stats.paused_us` panics in debug / wraps in release when paused_us exceeds elapsed (clock skew or as_micros truncation).

title: EventStream ignores max_drain limit
description: `next()` never checks/decrements `max_drain`, so `.with_max(n)` is silently no-op and iterator runs unbounded.

title: subscriber_count never decremented
description: EventReceiver has no Drop impl that decrements `subscriber_count`, so the reported count monotonically grows and misrepresents active subscribers.

title: replay_to only rewinds, doesn't replay
description: `replay_to` mutates next_seq under a shared RwLock read guard via interior Mutex — fine — but it does not actually replay buffered EventLog contents (only ring), so events outside ring capacity but in log are never delivered, contrary to docstring "Replay all buffered log events".

title: Publish holds persist_writer mutex during blocking file I/O
description: `writeln!` + `flush()` inside the locked Mutex serializes all publishers behind disk I/O, and a slow writer stalls the entire bus.

title: RingBuf capacity fallback allocates 2^63 slots
description: If `capacity.checked_next_power_of_two()` returns None, fallback `1 << (usize::BITS - 1)` attempts to allocate ~2^63 slots, OOM-panicking instead of erroring.

title: Replay duration subtraction can underflow
description: `start.elapsed().as_micros() as u64 - self.stats.paused_us` panics in debug or wraps in release when paused_us exceeds the truncated elapsed value.

title: subscriber_count never decremented
description: EventReceiver has no Drop that decrements `subscriber_count`, so the count grows monotonically and misreports active subscribers.

title: replay_to does not replay EventLog
